answer: Verifiable delay functions resist sybils: to stay active each identity must publish a VDF proof, a computation inherently sequential — no number of cores computes it faster, only wall-clock time does. One honest agent on its knoll runs a single glacier-slow chain and keeps pace. A farm of K identities needs K independent sequential chains advancing at once, since one machine cannot fold two VDF streams into one wall-clock. Reaching a summit of influence thus demands one sequential processor per fake; extra parallel hardware buys nothing. Precondition: the delay exceeds any shortcut.
